doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First playing in London, at Ronnie Scott's
summary: He recalls the all-night club and meeting Tubby Hayes and others, in 1968.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: When was the first time, do remember the first time that you played in London so that these British musicians could have actually seen you perform?

Well the first I played in London I played at this place that Ronnie Scott used to have. What’s the name of that street? The place they had before that? Anyway I’d go there, if we had a day off we’d go down there cause they stayed open all night. I met a lot of guys there. Tubby Hayes and all those guys.

’68, okay. But before that he had not played London? Okay so they go their style from you by listening to records. Because Mitch Mitchell in 1967 is already playing your style, he hadn’t seen you he just picked it up through his ears. One thing I wanted to check back with you on is 1967, the death of John Coltrane. Where were you, and how did you find out about it?
